avoid_supplements.name: St. John's Wort
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Potent CYP3A4 inducer reduces ritonavir plasma concentrations significantly, compromising antiretroviral efficacy
avoid_supplements.action: Contraindicated; do not use concurrently with ritonavir

avoid_supplements.name: Garlic supplements (high-dose)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: CYP3A4 induction may reduce ritonavir levels and increase protease inhibitor resistance risk
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid high-dose garlic supplements; counsel on use of culinary amounts only

avoid_supplements.name: Milk Thistle
avoid_supplements.mechanism: CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein induction may decrease ritonavir bioavailability
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid use; consider alternative liver support strategies if needed

avoid_supplements.name: Echinacea
avoid_supplements.mechanism: CYP3A4 induction potential may reduce ritonavir effectiveness
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid or use with caution; monitor viral load if concurrent use unavoidable

caution_supplements.name: Grapefruit seed extract
caution_supplements.mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibition may increase ritonavir levels; effect typically minimal with seed extract compared to juice
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for increased adverse effects; maintain consistent intake if used

caution_supplements.name: Omega-3 fatty acids
caution_supplements.mechanism: High doses may have anticoagulant effects; minimal direct interaction but monitor if combined with other anticoagulants
caution_supplements.action: Use at standard recommended doses; counsel on bleeding risk awareness

caution_supplements.name: Probiotics
caution_supplements.mechanism: No direct pharmacokinetic interaction; may support GI health during antiretroviral therapy
caution_supplements.action: Generally safe; may provide symptomatic benefit for GI side effects

avoid_foods.name: Grapefruit and grapefruit juice
avoid_foods.mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibition significantly increases ritonavir plasma concentrations and toxicity risk
avoid_foods.action: Contraindicated; advise complete avoidance including all grapefruit products

avoid_foods.name: High-fat meals (inconsistent intake)
avoid_foods.mechanism: Ritonavir absorption is food-dependent; inconsistent fat intake causes variable bioavailability affecting viral suppression
avoid_foods.action: Always take ritonavir with food (preferably meals containing fat >500 kcal); maintain consistent meal timing

caution_foods.name: Pomegranate juice
caution_foods.mechanism: Mild CYP3A4 inhibition; effect is generally minor compared to grapefruit
caution_foods.action: Moderate consumption acceptable; no strict avoidance required but monitor consistency

caution_foods.name: Seville orange (bitter orange)
caution_foods.mechanism: Potential CYP3A4 inhibition similar to but less potent than grapefruit
caution_foods.action: Limit consumption; prefer sweet oranges as safer alternative

caution_foods.name: Licorice-containing foods
caution_foods.mechanism: High doses may affect drug metabolism and electrolyte balance; minimal interaction at typical food intake levels
caution_foods.action: Use in moderation; avoid excessive licorice candy or supplements

monitoring_notes: Ritonavir is a potent CYP3A4 inhibitor used to boost other protease inhibitors; maintain consistent food intake (especially fat content) to ensure stable absorption and viral suppression. Monitor for signs of toxicity with CYP3A4-metabolized drugs and counsel on strict avoidance of enzyme-inducing supplements that compromise antiretroviral efficacy.
